title: Abelian Varieties, Base Change, and Arithmetic Models

items.title: Group schemes over a base scheme
items.statement: Let $S$ be a scheme. An $S$-group scheme is a group object in the category of $S$-schemes: an $S$-scheme $G$ together with $S$-morphisms $m:G\times_SG\to G$ (multiplication), $e:S\to G$ (unit section) and $i:G\to G$ (inverse) such that associativity, the two unit laws and the two inverse laws hold as identities of $S$-morphisms. A morphism of $S$-group schemes is an $S$-morphism compatible with $m,e,i$. Commutativity, closed subgroup schemes, normal subgroup schemes, kernels of morphisms, and the base change $G_{S'}=G\times_SS'$ with its induced $S'$-group structure are defined by the evident diagrams. This generalizes the field case of [[def-group-scheme-over-a-field]] and quotes no new existence statement.

items.title: Abelian schemes over a base
items.statement: Let $S$ be a scheme. An abelian scheme over $S$ of relative dimension $g$ is an $S$-group scheme $f:A\to S$ such that $f$ is smooth, proper and of finite presentation and every geometric fibre of $f$ is connected of dimension $g$. Equivalently, all fibres of $f$ are abelian varieties of dimension $g$ in the sense of [[def-abelian-variety-over-a-field]]; the relative dimension is locally constant on $S$ and equals $g$ on each connected component. The unit section $e:S\to A$ is a closed immersion and $A\to S$ is separated. No projectivity over $S$ is asserted; abelian schemes over a base need not be projective over that base.

items.title: Fibres of abelian schemes and unit-preserving morphisms
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $S$ be a scheme, let $A\to S$ and $B\to S$ be abelian schemes of relative dimensions $g_A,g_B$, and let $s\in S$. Then the fibre $A_s$ is an abelian variety of dimension $g_A$ over $\kappa(s)$; the multiplication of $A$ is commutative; the inversion of $A$ is the morphism $-1_A:A\to A$; and every $S$-morphism $u:A\to B$ with $u\circ e_A=e_B$ is a homomorphism of $S$-group schemes. Consequently, on a connected base, any two abelian-scheme structures on the same smooth proper $S$-scheme with the same unit section coincide. All assertions are fibrewise applications of the published rigidity and pointed-morphism results over the residue fields, together with the closedness of the unit section.

items.title: Base change and products of abelian schemes
items.statement: Let $A\to S$ and $B\to S$ be abelian schemes of relative dimensions $g_A,g_B$ and let $S'\to S$ be a morphism. Then the base change $A_{S'}=A\times_SS'\to S'$ is an abelian scheme of relative dimension $g_A$, its $S'$-group structure is induced by that of $A$, and for every $s'\in S'$ with image $s\in S$ the fibre $(A_{S'})_{s'}$ is the base change $A_s\times_{\kappa(s)}\kappa(s')$ of abelian varieties. Likewise $A\times_SB\to S$ is an abelian scheme of relative dimension $g_A+g_B$ with the product group law. The formation of kernels, images of homomorphisms and finite locally free subgroup schemes is compatible with base change.

items.title: Multiplication by n on an abelian scheme is finite flat, and etale for n invertible
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice and the Axiom of Dependent Choice, inherited from the finite-flatness and flatness-by-fibres suppliers. Let $S$ be locally Noetherian and let $A\to S$ be an abelian scheme of relative dimension $g$, let $n\ge1$, and let $[n]:A\to A$ be multiplication by $n$. Then $[n]$ is finite, flat and surjective of degree $n^{2g}$, and the kernel $A[n]=\ker[n]$ is a finite flat $S$-group scheme of rank $n^{2g}$. If $n$ is invertible on $S$, then $[n]$ is etale and $A[n]\to S$ is finite etale of rank $n^{2g}$. The proof is fibrewise: on every geometric fibre $[n]$ has finite kernel of order $n^{2g}$ by the published field-level theorem, so $[n]$ is quasi-finite and proper, hence finite, and flatness follows from constancy of the fibre rank by the Noetherian fibrewise flatness criterion; etaleness follows because the differential of $[n]$ at the unit is multiplication by the invertible scalar $n$ on the locally free sheaf of invariant differentials, and translations spread this everywhere.

references.title: S. Bosch, W. Lutkebohmert, M. items.title: Finite etale schemes over a complete discrete valuation ring with separably closed residue field are split
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $R$ be a Noetherian local ring complete and separated for its maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$, with residue field $k$, and let $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ be a finite etale $R$-scheme. Then reduction induces a bijection $Y(R)\to Y(k)$. If in addition $k$ is separably closed, then every finite etale $R$-algebra of rank $d$ is isomorphic to $R^{d}$ and $Y$ is a disjoint union of $d$ copies of $\operatorname{Spec}R$. The proof uses the lifting equivalence for finite etale algebras over complete local rings, which reduces the classification of finite etale $R$-algebras to that of finite etale $k$-algebras, and the fact that a finite etale algebra over a separably closed field is a product of copies of the field.

references.title: S. Bosch, W. Lutkebohmert, M. items.title: S-dense open subschemes and S-rational maps
items.statement: Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian scheme and let $X$ and $Y$ be smooth $S$-schemes. An open subscheme $U\subseteq X$ is $S$-dense if for every $s\in S$ the fibre $U_s$ is Zariski dense in $X_s$; finite intersections of $S$-dense opens are $S$-dense, and the restriction of an $S$-dense open to an open subscheme is $S$-dense there. An $S$-rational map $u:X\dashrightarrow Y$ is an equivalence class of $S$-morphisms $U\to Y$ defined on $S$-dense open subschemes, where two are equivalent if they agree on an $S$-dense open subscheme of the intersection. Equivalently, for every $s\in S$ one has a rational map $X_s\dashrightarrow Y_s$ of the fibres, compatible with specialisation; this is the relative notion of rational map that is compatible with base change and is used in the extension theorem [[thm-weil-extension-rational-map-into-group-scheme]]. The domain of definition is the largest $S$-dense open on which the class admits a representative, and it is compatible with base change.

references.title: S. Bosch, W. Lutkebohmert, M. Raynaud, Neron Models, Ergebnisse der Mathematik und ihrer Grenzgebiete (3) 21, Springer 1990 (Chapter 1 sections 1-2, Chapter 2 section 2.5, Chapter 3 sections 3.1-3.5, Chapter 4 sections 4.2-4.4, Chapter 7 section 7.2, Chapter 8 section 8.1, Chapter 10 section 10.2)

items.title: An S-rational map defined after a faithfully flat smooth base change is defined
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $S$ be locally Noetherian, let $u:X\dashrightarrow Y$ be an $S$-rational map between smooth finite-type $S$-schemes, and let $f:X'\to X$ be a faithfully flat morphism of smooth finite-type $S$-schemes such that the pullback $u\circ f:X'\dashrightarrow Y$ is represented by an $S$-morphism on all of $X'$. Then $u$ is represented by an $S$-morphism on all of $X$. The proof descends the representative of $u\circ f$ along the faithfully flat morphism $f$ using fppf descent of scheme morphisms; faithfulness of $f$ makes the descended morphism agree with every local representative of $u$ on an $S$-dense open.

references.title: S. Bosch, W. Lutkebohmert, M. Raynaud, Neron Models, Ergebnisse der Mathematik und ihrer Grenzgebiete (3) 21, Springer 1990 (Chapter 1 sections 1-2, Chapter 2 section 2.5, Chapter 3 sections 3.1-3.5, Chapter 4 sections 4.2-4.4, Chapter 7 section 7.2, Chapter 8 section 8.1, Chapter 10 section 10.2)

items.title: A normal Noetherian domain is the intersection of its height-one localizations
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $A$ be a Noetherian normal domain with fraction field $K$. Then inside $K$ one has $A=\bigcap_{\operatorname{ht}\mathfrak p=1}A_{\mathfrak p}$, the intersection running over the height-one prime ideals. Consequently a rational function on $\operatorname{Spec}A$ that is regular at every height-one point and at every generic point is regular everywhere; and for a normal Noetherian scheme $Z$ the indeterminacy locus of a rational map from $Z$ to an affine scheme is empty or has pure codimension one in every connected component.

references.title: S. Bosch, W. Lutkebohmert, M. Raynaud, Neron Models, Ergebnisse der Mathematik und ihrer Grenzgebiete (3) 21, Springer 1990 (Chapter 1 sections 1-2, Chapter 2 section 2.5, Chapter 3 sections 3.1-3.5, Chapter 4 sections 4.2-4.4, Chapter 7 section 7.2, Chapter 8 section 8.1, Chapter 10 section 10.2)
J. S. Milne, Abelian Varieties, v2.00 (2008), Chapter I sections 3, 5, 8, 11, 17

items.title: Indeterminacy of a rational map into an affine scheme is of pure codimension one
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $Z$ be a normal Noetherian scheme and let $u:Z\dashrightarrow\operatorname{Spec}B$ be a rational map to an affine scheme. Then the indeterminacy locus of $u$ is empty or has pure codimension one in every connected component of $Z$; in particular, if $u$ is defined at every point of height at most one, then $u$ extends uniquely to a morphism $Z\to\operatorname{Spec}B$. The proof restricts to an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq Z$ and applies the intersection description of the normal domain $A$ to each coordinate function of $u$.

references.title: S. Bosch, W. Lutkebohmert, M. Raynaud, Neron Models, Ergebnisse der Mathematik und ihrer Grenzgebiete (3) 21, Springer 1990 (Chapter 1 sections 1-2, Chapter 2 section 2.5, Chapter 3 sections 3.1-3.5, Chapter 4 sections 4.2-4.4, Chapter 7 section 7.2, Chapter 8 section 8.1, Chapter 10 section 10.2)

items.title: Weil's extension theorem for rational maps into smooth separated group schemes
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice and the Axiom of Dependent Choice, inherited from the descent and purity suppliers. Let $S$ be a normal Noetherian base scheme, let $Z$ be a smooth $S$-scheme, and let $G$ be a smooth separated $S$-group scheme of finite type. If an $S$-rational map $u:Z\dashrightarrow G$ is defined in codimension $\le1$, that is, at every height-one point of $Z$, then $u$ is defined everywhere and extends uniquely to an $S$-morphism $Z\to G$. Proof strategy (BLR 4.4/1): form the rational map $v:Z\times_SZ\dashrightarrow G$, $(z_1,z_2)\mapsto u(z_1)u(z_2)^{-1}$, use the group law to see that $v$ is defined on the diagonal where $u$ is defined; near a diagonal point choose an affine neighbourhood $H$ of the unit in $G$ and apply the pure-codimension-one lemma to the composite into $H$ to show that the indeterminacy of $v$ misses the diagonal because the diagonal is cut out by $d=\operatorname{rel.dim}(Z/S)$ equations in the smooth (hence normal) scheme $Z\times_SZ$. Then $Z':=V\cap(Z\times_SU)$ (with $U$ the domain of $u$ and $V$ the domain of $v$) is smooth over $S$, the first projection $Z'\to Z$ is faithfully flat and surjective, and $u\circ\operatorname{pr}_1=v|_{Z'}$ is defined everywhere, so the descent lemma gives that $u$ is defined everywhere. Uniqueness follows from separatedness of $G$.

references.title: S. Bosch, W. Lutkebohmert, M. Raynaud, Neron Models, Ergebnisse der Mathematik und ihrer Grenzgebiete (3) 21, Springer 1990 (Chapter 1 sections 1-2, Chapter 2 section 2.5, Chapter 3 sections 3.1-3.5, Chapter 4 sections 4.2-4.4, Chapter 7 section 7.2, Chapter 8 section 8.1, Chapter 10 section 10.2)
J. S. Milne, Abelian Varieties, v2.00 (2008), Chapter I sections 3, 5, 8, 11, 17

items.title: K-morphisms from smooth models into abelian schemes extend uniquely
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $S$ be a Dedekind scheme with function field $K$, let $A\to S$ be an abelian scheme, and let $Z\to S$ be a smooth $S$-scheme of finite type. Then restriction along $Z_K=Z\times_S\operatorname{Spec}K\hookrightarrow Z$ is a bijection $$\operatorname{Hom}_S(Z,A)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}_K(Z_K,A_K).$$ In particular, for every closed point $s\in S$ and every generic point $\xi$ of the fibre $Z_s$ the local ring $\mathcal O_{Z,\xi}$ is a discrete valuation ring whose fraction field is the function field $K(Z)$ of $Z$, a field containing $K$; a given $K$-morphism $Z_K\to A_K$ therefore yields a $K(Z)$-point of $A$, and the valuative criterion of properness for $A/S$ extends it over $\mathcal O_{Z,\xi}$; it is therefore defined in codimension $\le1$, and Weil's extension theorem applies. This is the extension statement used to identify abelian schemes as Neron models.

references.title: S. Bosch, W. Lutkebohmert, M. Raynaud, Neron Models, Ergebnisse der Mathematik und ihrer Grenzgebiete (3) 21, Springer 1990 (Chapter 1 sections 1-2, Chapter 2 section 2.5, Chapter 3 sections 3.1-3.5, Chapter 4 sections 4.2-4.4, Chapter 7 section 7.2, Chapter 8 section 8.1, Chapter 10 section 10.2)
J. S. Milne, Abelian Varieties, v2.00 (2008), Chapter I sections 3, 5, 8, 11, 17

items.title: Neron models and the Neron mapping property
items.statement: Let $S$ be a Dedekind scheme with function field $K$, and let $X_K$ be a smooth separated $K$-scheme of finite type. A Neron model of $X_K$ over $S$ is an $S$-model $X\to S$ which is smooth, separated and of finite type, and which satisfies the Neron mapping property: for every smooth $S$-scheme $Y$ and every $K$-morphism $u_K:Y_K\to X_K$ there is a unique $S$-morphism $u:Y\to X$ extending $u_K$. When $S$ is local, the local Neron model at the closed point is $X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{S,s}$. A weak Neron model is a smooth separated finite-type model satisfying the extension property for etale points, namely that every $R'$-valued point of $X_K$, for every finite etale extension of local rings $R\subseteq R'$ of $S$, extends to $X$. The Neron mapping property for $Y=X$ shows that a Neron model is determined by its generic fibre up to a unique isomorphism; no existence is asserted by this definition.

references.title: S. Bosch, W. Lutkebohmert, M. Raynaud, Neron Models, Ergebnisse der Mathematik und ihrer Grenzgebiete (3) 21, Springer 1990 (Chapter 1 sections 1-2, Chapter 2 section 2.5, Chapter 3 sections 3.1-3.5, Chapter 4 sections 4.2-4.4, Chapter 7 section 7.2, Chapter 8 section 8.1, Chapter 10 section 10.2)
D. Lombardo, Abelian varieties, Luxembourg Summer School on Galois representations lecture notes (2018), Chapter 1 sections 1-7 and Chapter 2 sections 4-5
J. S. Milne, Abelian Varieties, v2.00 (2008), Chapter I sections 3, 5, 8, 11, 17

items.title: Uniqueness, weak Neron property, etale base change and local nature of Neron models
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $S$ be a Dedekind scheme with function field $K$ and let $X$ be a Neron model of the smooth separated finite-type $K$-scheme $X_K$. Then: (a) $X$ is unique up to a unique $S$-isomorphism; (b) $X$ is a weak Neron model: it satisfies the extension property for etale points, since the Neron mapping property applies to etale $Y$; (c) for every etale morphism $S'\to S$ with function field $K'$, the base change $X_{S'}$ is a Neron model of $X_{K'}$; (d) $X$ is a Neron model if and only if $X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{S,s}$ is a Neron model over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{S,s}$ for every closed point $s\in S$, and Neron models are local on the base; (e) if $X_K$ is a $K$-group scheme then the group law extends uniquely to $X$, making $X$ an $S$-group scheme. The arguments apply the mapping property directly, with limit arguments reducing morphisms of finite presentation over localizations to a neighbourhood of the point.

references.title: S. Bosch, W. Lutkebohmert, M. Raynaud, Neron Models, Ergebnisse der Mathematik und ihrer Grenzgebiete (3) 21, Springer 1990 (Chapter 1 sections 1-2, Chapter 2 section 2.5, Chapter 3 sections 3.1-3.5, Chapter 4 sections 4.2-4.4, Chapter 7 section 7.2, Chapter 8 section 8.1, Chapter 10 section 10.2)
J. S. Milne, Abelian Varieties, v2.00 (2008), Chapter I sections 3, 5, 8, 11, 17

items.title: An abelian scheme is the Neron model of its generic fibre
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $S$ be a Dedekind scheme with function field $K$ and let $A\to S$ be an abelian scheme. Then $A$ is a Neron model of its generic fibre $A_K$: for every smooth $S$-scheme $Y$ and every $K$-morphism $u_K:Y_K\to A_K$ there is a unique $S$-morphism $Y\to A$ extending $u_K$. Proof strategy (BLR 1.2/8): fix a closed point $s\in S$ and a generic point $\xi$ of the fibre $Y_s$; then $\mathcal O_{Y,\xi}$ is a discrete valuation ring whose fraction field is the function field $K(Y)$, a field containing $K$, the given $K$-morphism yields a $K(Y)$-point of $A$, and the valuative criterion of properness for the proper morphism $A\to S$ extends it over $\xi$. Hence the resulting $S$-rational map is defined in codimension $\le1$ and Weil's extension theorem makes it a morphism; uniqueness is separatedness of $A$. The abelian scheme is thus a weak Neron model, and the criterion [[lem-neron-model-uniqueness-etale-base-change-and-local-nature]] upgrades it to a Neron model using the group structure of $A_K$.

references.title: S. Bosch, W. Lutkebohmert, M. Raynaud, Neron Models, Ergebnisse der Mathematik und ihrer Grenzgebiete (3) 21, Springer 1990 (Chapter 1 sections 1-2, Chapter 2 section 2.5, Chapter 3 sections 3.1-3.5, Chapter 4 sections 4.2-4.4, Chapter 7 section 7.2, Chapter 8 section 8.1, Chapter 10 section 10.2)
J. S. Milne, Abelian Varieties, v2.00 (2008), Chapter I sections 3, 5, 8, 11, 17
D. Lombardo, Abelian varieties, Luxembourg Summer School on Galois representations lecture notes (2018), Chapter 1 sections 1-7 and Chapter 2 sections 4-5

items.title: Good reduction of an abelian variety over a Dedekind scheme
items.statement: Let $S$ be a Dedekind scheme with function field $K$, and let $A_K$ be an abelian variety over $K$. One says that $A_K$ has good reduction over $S$ if there exists an abelian scheme $A\to S$ together with an isomorphism $A\times_S\operatorname{Spec}K\cong A_K$. For a discrete valuation ring $R$ with fraction field $K$ this is the local notion; $A_K$ has potential good reduction if $A_K\otimes_KK'$ has good reduction over the normalization of $R$ in $K'$ for some finite extension $K'/K$. By [[thm-abelian-scheme-is-the-neron-model-of-its-generic-fibre]] an abelian scheme model, when it exists, is the Neron model of its generic fibre, and by [[cor-extension-of-k-morphisms-into-abelian-schemes]] two such models are canonically isomorphic; the reduction $A_s=A\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ is an abelian variety over $\kappa(s)$. Good reduction is a property of the pair $(A_K,S)$; no claim is made that every abelian variety has good reduction.

references.title: S. Bosch, W. Lutkebohmert, M. Raynaud, Neron Models, Ergebnisse der Mathematik und ihrer Grenzgebiete (3) 21, Springer 1990 (Chapter 1 sections 1-2, Chapter 2 section 2.5, Chapter 3 sections 3.1-3.5, Chapter 4 sections 4.2-4.4, Chapter 7 section 7.2, Chapter 8 section 8.1, Chapter 10 section 10.2)

items.title: Good reduction supplies a Neron model
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $S$ be a Dedekind scheme with function field $K$ and let $A_K$ be an abelian variety over $K$ with good reduction over $S$. Then $A_K$ admits a Neron model over $S$, namely any abelian scheme model $A\to S$ of $A_K$, and this model is unique up to a unique $S$-isomorphism. In particular, for a discrete valuation ring $R$ with fraction field $K$, every abelian variety over $K$ with good reduction has a Neron model over $R$, and the Neron model in this class is proper and smooth over $R$.

references.title: S. Bosch, W. Lutkebohmert, M. Raynaud, Neron Models, Ergebnisse der Mathematik und ihrer Grenzgebiete (3) 21, Springer 1990 (Chapter 1 sections 1-2, Chapter 2 section 2.5, Chapter 3 sections 3.1-3.5, Chapter 4 sections 4.2-4.4, Chapter 7 section 7.2, Chapter 8 section 8.1, Chapter 10 section 10.2)
D. Lombardo, Abelian varieties, Luxembourg Summer School on Galois representations lecture notes (2018), Chapter 1 sections 1-7 and Chapter 2 sections 4-5

items.title: Good reduction is stable under base change of the base
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $S$ be a Dedekind scheme with function field $K$, let $A_K$ be an abelian variety with good reduction over $S$ witnessed by an abelian scheme $A\to S$, and let $S'\to S$ be a morphism of Dedekind schemes with function field $K'$ (for instance the normalization of $S$ in a finite extension $K'/K$, or the localisation of $S$ at a point). Then $A_{S'}\to S'$ is an abelian scheme and $A_{K'}=A_{S'}\times_{S'}\operatorname{Spec}K'$ has good reduction over $S'$; the model $A_{S'}$ is the base change of the model $A$. In particular good reduction is preserved by finite extensions of the function field and by localisation of the base. Nothing is asserted here about the converse direction; the example and counterexample items on the companion page record the failure of descent along ramified base change.

references.title: S. Bosch, W. Lutkebohmert, M. Raynaud, Neron Models, Ergebnisse der Mathematik und ihrer Grenzgebiete (3) 21, Springer 1990 (Chapter 1 sections 1-2, Chapter 2 section 2.5, Chapter 3 sections 3.1-3.5, Chapter 4 sections 4.2-4.4, Chapter 7 section 7.2, Chapter 8 section 8.1, Chapter 10 section 10.2)
J. S. Milne, Abelian Varieties, v2.00 (2008), Chapter I sections 3, 5, 8, 11, 17
D. Lombardo, Abelian varieties, Luxembourg Summer School on Galois representations lecture notes (2018), Chapter 1 sections 1-7 and Chapter 2 sections 4-5

items.title: Good reduction and smooth proper base change for abelian schemes
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice and the Axiom of Dependent Choice, inherited from the cohomology-and-base-change suppliers. Let $S$ be a Dedekind scheme with function field $K$, let $f:A\to S$ be an abelian scheme of relative dimension $g$, and let $A_K$ be its generic fibre. Then: (a) [good reduction] $A_K$ is an abelian variety with good reduction over $S$, the abelian scheme model $A$ is unique up to a unique $S$-isomorphism, and $A$ is the Neron model of $A_K$; for every closed point $s\in S$ the fibre $A_s$ is an abelian variety of dimension $g$ over $\kappa(s)$. (b) [base change] For every morphism $S'\to S$ the base change $A_{S'}\to S'$ is an abelian scheme of relative dimension $g$, it represents the base change of the good reduction data, and if $S'$ is a Dedekind scheme with function field $K'$ then $A_{K'}$ has good reduction over $S'$. (c) [smooth proper base change] Fix $s\in S$, $q\ge0$ and a coherent $\mathcal O_A$-module $\mathcal F$ flat over $S$, and let $\varphi_s^q:(R^qf_*\mathcal F)(s)\to H^q(A_s,\mathcal F_s)$ be the cohomology-and-base-change map. If $\varphi_s^q$ is surjective, then there is an affine open neighbourhood $U\subseteq S$ of $s$ such that for every $T\to U$ the base-change map $h^*(R^qf_*\mathcal F|_U)\to R^qf'_{T*}(g_T^*\mathcal F)$ is an isomorphism; if moreover $\varphi_s^{q-1}$ is surjective, then $R^qf_*\mathcal F$ is finite locally free on a neighbourhood of $s$. For $q=0$ and $\mathcal F=\mathcal O_A$ the map $f_*\mathcal O_A\to\mathcal O_S$ is an isomorphism, and for $\mathcal F$ a line bundle flat over $S$ the higher direct images are finite locally free wherever the successive base-change maps are surjective. (d) [residue restrictions] No restriction on the residue characteristic of $S$ is imposed in (a)-(c); the finite flatness conclusions in (c) are stated under the exact surjectivity hypotheses of the cohomology-and-base-change theorem, because fibrewise cohomology of smooth proper families need not be locally constant in residue characteristic $p>0$. The etale-cohomological refinement of (a), the Neron-Ogg-Shafarevich criterion, is not proved here; it is recorded as deferred in the batch notes since it requires the etale cohomology and l-adic Tate module foundations, which are not available in the library.

items.title: Existence of Neron models for abelian varieties over a discrete valuation ring
items.statement: Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring with fraction field $K$ and residue field $k$, and let $A_K$ be an abelian variety over $K$ (smooth, proper, geometrically connected). Then $A_K$ admits a Neron model over $R$: there is a smooth separated finite-type $R$-group scheme $\mathcal A$ whose generic fibre is $A_K$ and which satisfies the Neron mapping property for all smooth $R$-schemes. Equivalently $\mathcal A(R^{\mathrm{sh}})$-points of the generic fibre extend, and $\mathcal A$ is unique up to a unique $R$-isomorphism. BLR prove the more general local existence theorem: for a smooth finite-type $K$-group scheme $X_K$, a Neron model over $R$ exists if and only if $X_K(K^{\mathrm{sh}})$ is bounded in $X_K$; abelian varieties are proper, hence bounded, giving the stated corollary. The proof of the general theorem occupies BLR Chapters 3-6 (smoothening of a separated model via Neron's measure, construction of an $R$-birational group law from the invariant differential, Weil's theorem on birational group laws over a strictly henselian base, and descent to a general discrete valuation ring), together with the criterion of BLR 1.2/19.

items.title: The rigidified relative Picard functor and the dual abelian variety
items.statement: Let $f:A\to S$ be an abelian scheme with unit section $e:S\to A$. The rigidified relative Picard functor $\mathcal P_{A/S,e}$ is the fppf sheaf on $(\mathrm{Sch}/S)$ associated with the functor sending an $S$-scheme $T$ to the set of isomorphism classes of pairs $(\mathcal L,\alpha)$, where $\mathcal L$ is an invertible sheaf on $A_T$ and $\alpha:\mathcal O_T\to e_T^*\mathcal L$ is a trivialisation along the unit section, with group law given by tensor product. An $S$-scheme representing $\mathcal P_{A/S,e}$ is called a relative Picard scheme; its identity component is denoted $\operatorname{Pic}^0_{A/S}$ and, when it exists and is an abelian variety, is called the dual abelian variety $\hat A$ of $A$. A Poincare sheaf is the universal rigidified invertible sheaf $\mathcal P$ on $A\times_S\hat A$. The degree-zero part of the functor on the fibres is defined by restricting isomorphism classes of line bundles that lie in the connected component of the identity; it is a group functor. This definition records the functor and the universal property only; no representability is asserted here, and the existence statement is [[thm-abelian-variety-dual-and-polarization]].

items.title: The theorem of the square and the Mumford homomorphism into the Picard group
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $A$ be an abelian variety over a field $k$, let $\mathcal L$ be an invertible sheaf on $A$, and let $t_a:A\to A$ denote translation by $a\in A(k'')$ for a field extension $k''/k$. Then the theorem of the square holds: $$t_{a+b}^*\mathcal L\otimes\mathcal L\;\cong\;t_a^*\mathcal L\otimes t_b^*\mathcal L$$ for all $a,b\in A(k'')$, and the formula is functorial in $k''$. Consequently the Mumford map $$\varphi_{\mathcal L}:A(k'')\longrightarrow\operatorname{Pic}(A_{k''}),\qquad a\longmapsto[t_a^*\mathcal L\otimes\mathcal L^{-1}],$$ is a homomorphism of groups and lands in the degree-zero part of the rigidified Picard functor; it is compatible with field extension. The proof derives the square formula by specialising the published theorem of the cube to the three maps $1_A,a,b:A\to A$, exactly as in Milne I.5.5-I.5.6.

items.title: Polarizations and the Mumford isogeny attached to an ample line bundle
items.statement: Let $A$ be an abelian variety over a field $k$ with dual abelian variety $\hat A$ (the representing object of the degree-zero part of the rigidified Picard functor, whose existence is [[thm-abelian-variety-dual-and-polarization]]) and Poincare sheaf $\mathcal P$ on $A\times_k\hat A$. For an invertible sheaf $\mathcal L$ on $A$ the Mumford homomorphism $\varphi_{\mathcal L}:A\to\hat A$ is the unique homomorphism with $(1,\varphi_{\mathcal L})^*\mathcal P\cong m^*\mathcal L\otimes p_1^*\mathcal L^{-1}\otimes p_2^*\mathcal L^{-1}$, and on points it is $a\mapsto[t_a^*\mathcal L\otimes\mathcal L^{-1}]$. A polarization of $A$ is a symmetric homomorphism $\lambda:A\to\hat A$, meaning $\lambda=\lambda^\vee$ under the canonical identification $A\cong\hat{\hat A}$, such that the invertible sheaf $(1,\lambda)^*\mathcal P$ on $A$ is ample. A principal polarization is a polarization of degree $1$. The definition records the symmetry, amplitude and degree conditions precisely; the theorem that $\varphi_{\mathcal L}$ is an isogeny for $\mathcal L$ ample, and the existence of $\hat A$, are part of the escalated item [[thm-abelian-variety-dual-and-polarization]].

items.title: The dual abelian variety, the Poincare bundle and polarizations
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $A$ be an abelian variety over a field $k$, of dimension $g$. Then: (a) [existence and duality] the degree-zero part of the rigidified relative Picard functor of $A/k$ is representable by an abelian variety $\hat A$, the dual abelian variety, of dimension $g$, with universal Poincare sheaf $\mathcal P$ on $A\times_k\hat A$; the canonical homomorphism $A\to\hat{\hat A}$ is an isomorphism; (b) [functoriality] $A\mapsto\hat A$ is a contravariant functor on abelian varieties over $k$, and for every isogeny $f:A\to B$ the dual $f^\vee:\hat B\to\hat A$ is an isogeny with kernel the Cartier dual of $\ker f$; (c) [Mumford maps] for every invertible sheaf $\mathcal L$ on $A$ the Mumford homomorphism $\varphi_{\mathcal L}:A\to\hat A$ exists; if $\mathcal L$ is ample then $\varphi_{\mathcal L}$ is an isogeny with finite kernel $K(\mathcal L)$, and every symmetric homomorphism $A\to\hat A$ is $\varphi_{\mathcal L}$ for some invertible sheaf $\mathcal L$ after base change to a separably closed field; (d) [polarizations] an ample $\mathcal L$ makes $\varphi_{\mathcal L}$ a polarization, every abelian variety admits a polarization, the degree of a polarization is a perfect square, and $A$ is projective.

items.title: The chord-tangent group law on a smooth short Weierstrass cubic
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited from the Riemann-Roch and Serre duality suppliers. Let $k$ be a field of characteristic not $2$ or $3$, let $a,b\in k$ with $4a^3+27b^2
eq0$, and let $C\subset\mathbf P^2_k$ be the plane cubic $Y^2Z=X^3+aXZ^2+bZ^3$ with the rational point $O=[0:1:0]$. Then the chord-tangent construction defines a group law on $C$ with identity $O$, and $C$ together with this law is an abelian variety over $k$. In affine coordinates $y^2=x^3+ax+b$ the law is computed by the two regular expressions for the chord slope, $\lambda=(y_2-y_1)/(x_2-x_1)=(x_1^2+x_1x_2+x_2^2+a)/(y_1+y_2)$, valid on the respective opens $x_1
eq x_2$ and $y_1+y_2
eq0$, with $x(P+Q)=\lambda^2-x_1-x_2$ and $y(P+Q)=\lambda(x_1-x(P+Q))-y_1$; the union of the two opens is the complement of the single closed locus $x_1=x_2,\ y_1=0$, namely the doubling of a two-torsion point, where $2P=O$. Proof strategy: the cubic is a smooth proper geometrically integral genus-one curve with a rational point, so the full Riemann-Roch theorem and Serre duality give a bijection $C(k')	o\operatorname{Pic}^0(C_{k'})$, $P\mapsto[\mathcal O(P-O)]$, for every extension $k'/k$, and transporting the group structure of $\operatorname{Pic}^0$ gives the unique group law with identity $O$; the group axioms are checked on geometric points by the classical chord-tangent divisor computation. Algebraicity is checked by covering $C	imes_kC$ by the two opens above and the closed locus $x_1=x_2$, $y_1=0$ mapping to $O$: the two slope expressions agree on the overlap $(x_1-x_2)(y_1+y_2)
eq0$ as polynomial identity using $y_i^2=x_i^3+ax_i+b$, the resulting map lands on $C$, and the three locally defined morphisms glue to a morphism $C	imes_kC	o C$. Inverse is $[X:Y:Z]\mapsto[X:-Y:Z]$ and the group axioms follow from the pointwise group law plus reducedness of the products and separatedness of $C$.

items.title: Two-torsion and uniqueness of the group law on a Weierstrass cubic
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $k$ be a field of characteristic not $2$ or $3$, let $a,b\in k$ with $4a^3+27b^2\neq0$, and let $C$ be the smooth cubic $Y^2Z=X^3+aXZ^2+bZ^3$ with $O=[0:1:0]$, regarded as an abelian variety by [[thm-plane-cubic-chord-tangent-group-law]]. Then: (a) the two-torsion subgroup of $C$ consists exactly of $O$ together with the three points $[x:0:1]$ with $x^3+ax+b=0$; in particular $C[2](k)=\{O\}$ if and only if the cubic $x^3+ax+b$ has no root in $k$; (b) if $C$ carries any abelian-variety structure with unit section $O$, then that group law equals the chord-tangent law, because the identity morphism from $(C,\cdot)$ to $(C,*)$ preserves the unit and is therefore a homomorphism by the pointed-morphism theorem, and its inverse gives the reverse implication. The inflection computation proves (a): a point $[x:y:1]$ with $y\neq0$ has vertical tangent only if $y=0$, and the chord-tangent doubling law shows that $2P=O$ exactly at the inflection points, which for the short Weierstrass form are the points with $y=0$.

title: Abelian Varieties, Base Change, and Arithmetic Models — Examples

items.title: An elliptic curve with good reduction and an elliptic curve with bad reduction
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice and Dependent Choice as inherited from the supplied local items. (a) [good] Let $E_0$ be the complex elliptic curve of [[ex-elliptic-curve-as-nonaffine-algebraic-group]] (a smooth projective cubic over $\mathbf C$ with the chord-tangent group law), let $R=\mathbf C[[t]]$, $K=\mathbf C((t))$, and let $A=E_0\times_{\mathbf C}R$ be the constant base change. Then $A\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is an abelian scheme of relative dimension $1$ with generic fibre $E_0\otimes_{\mathbf C}K$; by [[thm-abelian-scheme-is-the-neron-model-of-its-generic-fibre]] $A$ is the Neron model of its generic fibre, so the generic fibre has good reduction over $R$ and its special fibre is $E_0$. (b) [bad] Let $k$ be a field of characteristic not $2$ or $3$ with $k$ algebraically closed, let $R=k[[t]]$, $K=k((t))$, and let $E_t$ be the smooth cubic $Y^2Z=X^3+tZ^3$ with $O=[0:1:0]$, an elliptic curve over $K$ by [[thm-plane-cubic-chord-tangent-group-law]]. Then $E_t$ has bad reduction over $R$: there is no abelian scheme $A\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ with generic fibre $E_t$. Indeed, if such $A$ existed, then multiplication by $2$ would be finite etale of rank $4$ by [[lem-multiplication-by-n-on-abelian-scheme]], so $A[2]$ would be finite etale over $R$; by [[lem-finite-etale-lifting-over-complete-dvr]] reduction $A[2](R)\to A[2](k)$ would be bijective with $A[2](k)=\mathbf Z/2\times\mathbf Z/2$ (the special fibre is an elliptic curve in characteristic not $2$), hence $A[2](K)=E_t[2](K)$ would have $4$ elements. But the two-torsion of $E_t$ is computed by [[lem-two-torsion-and-uniqueness-of-plane-cubic-group-law]] as $\{O\}$ together with the roots in $K$ of $x^3+t=0$, and $x^3+t$ is Eisenstein at $t$, so it has no root in $K=k((t))$; thus $E_t[2](K)=\{O\}$, a contradiction. (c) The contrast in (b) is sharp: over the totally ramified extension $k((s))$ with $s^6=t$ the substitution $x=s^2x'$, $y=s^3y'$ identifies $E_t\otimes_k((t))\,k((s))$ with $Y^2Z=X^3+Z^3$, the base change from $k$ of an elliptic curve with good reduction, so $E_t$ has bad reduction over $k[[t]]$ but acquires good reduction after a finite ramified extension.

items.title: Not every abelian variety over a Dedekind function field extends to an abelian scheme
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice and Dependent Choice as inherited. There exist a Dedekind scheme $S$, a function field $K$ and an abelian variety $A_K$ over $K$ such that $A_K$ admits no abelian scheme model, i.e. no good reduction, over $S$. Explicitly, for $k$ algebraically closed of characteristic not $2$ or $3$, $R=k[[t]]$, $K=k((t))$, the elliptic curve $E_t:Y^2Z=X^3+tZ^3$ over $K$ with origin $O=[0:1:0]$ has no abelian scheme model over $R$: if $A\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ were one, then the finite etale group scheme $A[2]$ of rank $4$ would satisfy $A[2](K)\to A[2](k)$ bijective with target of order $4$, whereas the two-torsion of $A_K=E_t$ is the set $\{O\}\cup\{\text{roots of }x^3+t\}$, which is a single point because $x^3+t$ is Eisenstein over $k[[t]]$. This contradicts the general principle that good reduction can be tested on torsion of order invertible on the base. The same computation shows that the set of places of good reduction is not all of the base unless it is spread out, and that good reduction is not in general obtainable by arbitrary finite ramified base change descent.
